scholarships.title: Maria Leptin | EMBO Science Journalism Fellowships

eligibility: Applicants must reside in an EMBC Member State
The placement or placements must also occur in an EMBC Member State
Placements must be in person; virtual placements are not eligible
If Fellows undertake two or more placements, at least one must be in a different EMBC Member State than the others
Applicants are not subject to any age restriction
Journalists must demonstrate relevant experience of working as an employed or freelance journalist as their main occupation
Journalists must provide samples of their published or broadcast work
Journalists must show a genuine desire to broaden and deepen their knowledge of science, not a search for immediate publication opportunities
Life scientists seeking to transition to full-time journalism must hold a master's degree or higher, preferably in a life sciences discipline
Life scientists must demonstrate a genuine intention to move into journalism as a profession, with evidence of prior reporting on the life sciences or associated disciplines
Personal blog posts, social media postings, or commentary and review articles in academic journals are not accepted as evidence of prior journalism
Fellows are expected not to undertake other work during the fellowship and must not report on their host research institution during the fellowship term
existing.eligibility_summary: Either an employed or freelance working journalist with demonstrable relevant experience and samples of published or broadcast work who wants to deepen their science knowledge, or a life scientist with a master's degree or higher who wants to transition into full-time science journalism and has prior reporting on the life sciences.
benefits: Daily subsistence stipend sized to the cost of living in the host country
Travel costs connected with the placement
coverage: Daily subsistence stipend sized to the cost of living in the host country
Travel costs connected with the placement
requirements: Proposal in English of a maximum of three pages
For journalists: nomination of the research institution and specific learning and knowledge outcomes
For researchers: nomination of the newsroom and confirmation that the placement will be a full-time internship producing published or broadcast science journalism
Curriculum vitae in English with permanent residential address, email and mobile phone number
Samples of previous journalism work, which may be in any language
Prior discussion of the proposal with the proposed host, although formal written acceptance is not required at application stage
For journalists: confirmation that the sabbatical is focused on individual learning and long-term development and that the fellow will not report from the host institution
documents: Proposal in English, maximum three pages
CV in English including permanent residential address, email and mobile contact
Samples of previous journalism work in any language
Journalists only: statement that the sabbatical is focused on learning and that they will not report from the host institution
Researchers only: written confirmation that the proposed placement is a full-time internship in a mainstream media newsroom
existing.english_requirement: The proposal and curriculum vitae must be in English; samples of journalism work may be in any language.
application_method: Online application through the EMBO application portal only; only fully completed applications are considered
Successful applicants organise their own placements and receive a conditional offer subject to final confirmation from the host institution or newsroom
existing.selection_notes: Selection takes place once a year, with outcomes notified by email by mid-November. Applicants are judged by the EMBO advisory board on the genuine desire to broaden science knowledge or to move into journalism, the quality of the proposal and the learning outcomes set. The scheme was made possible by a private donation from Professor Maria Leptin.
existing.best_fit: Working science journalists based in EMBC Member States who want an in-person research sabbatical, and mid-career life scientists with a master's or doctorate who have already begun reporting and want to move into full-time science journalism in a mainstream newsroom.
existing.notes: The fellowship cannot be extended. Fellows are responsible for their own social security contributions, taxes and other costs. Both the applicant and the placement must be in an EMBC Member State, so this scheme cannot be used from outside Europe or for a placement outside Europe.
existing.duration: Journalists: minimum three months, maximum six months. Researchers transitioning to journalism: minimum three months, maximum twelve months.
existing.application_period: Applications can be submitted at any time; selection takes place once a year and fully completed applications must be registered in the EMBO portal by 23:59 CEST on 30 October each year. Applicants are notified by mid-November.
existing.deadline_display: 30 October each year, 23:59 Central European Summer Time (applications may be submitted at any time but must be registered by this deadline)
